keyFindings.description: The carry rule became `other === null || dispatchUrl === undefined || other === dispatchUrl`. Recording the targeted URL at :443 already fixes the failing-token case with the strict comparison `outcome.dispatch_url === (dispatchUrl ?? null)`; the two extra branches add new behaviour. (a) While envoy.json cannot be read (the hook's dispatchUrl is undefined), a refresher that targeted another Dispatch hands its list to the hook, shown as fresh: the list from another Dispatch URL the architect required never to stand in. (b) A refresher that ran while envoy.json was broken (dispatch_url null) hands its stale failure line to a hook for Dispatch A, so A's cached list is dropped. Reproduced by both thermonuclear agents against the committed bundle (/legion/scratch/tmp/r5-repro.ts); the round-4 bundle behaved correctly in both. No test reaches either branch.

Acceptance note: the 800 ms value is no longer pinned (printDeadline and notFinishedReason use the imported constant), and DEADLINE_SLACK_MS = 1000 lets the hook print and exit up to 1,000 ms past its deadline.

Acceptance note: the tests-only timing-file write is outside the try, so an unwritable ENVOY_ANSWERS_TIMING_FILE makes the hook exit 1 after printing. Unset in production, so nothing is written there.
